introduction: Start with the three calculator-allowed tech-active practice exams, written with new questions in the style of your past exams. Each has short answer, multiple choice and extended response sections worth 60 marks. Then use the textbook topic checklist to identify topics to revise. The Gauss notes and two Gauss papers are optional enrichment: paper 1 uses worked examples (answers also appear in the Notes, so try them first); paper 2 uses exercises with the book’s worked solutions.

notes.heading: Gauss — Arithmetic sequences and series
notes.body:
An arithmetic sequence is an ordered list of numbers that increase by the same fixed amount, called the common difference.
The common difference can be negative: {13, 7, 1, −5, …} has d = −6, so the “increase” is negative.
With first term a and common difference d: tₙ = a + (n − 1)d.
The sum of the first n terms is Sₙ = n/2 × (2a + (n − 1)d).
Example 1: {1, 4, 7, 10, …}; a = 1, d = 3; t₁₀₀ = 1 + 99 × 3 = 298.
Example 2: t₈ = 50 and t₂₀ = 14. Subtracting a + 7d = 50 and a + 19d = 14 gives 12d = −36, d = −3, a = 71.
Example 3: {13, 7, 1, −5, …}; S₄₉ = 49/2 × (2 × 13 + 48 × (−6)) = −6419.
notes.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.1–2

notes.heading: Gauss — Geometric sequences
notes.body:
A sequence is geometric if tₙ₊₁ = r tₙ for a fixed common ratio r. With first term a, tₙ = arⁿ⁻¹.
Example 4: {768, 384, 192, …}; r = 1/2; t₁₅ = 768 × (1/2)¹⁴ = 3/64.
Example 5: t₂₀ = 24 and t₂₃ = 648. Dividing gives r³ = 27, so r = 3.
Example 6: {…, 5, x, 245, …}; 5r² = 245, so r = 7 or −7 and x = 35 or −35.
notes.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.3–4

notes.heading: Gauss — Prime decomposition and counting factors
notes.body:
Every integer greater than 1 is either a prime or a product of two or more primes; the prime decomposition is unique apart from order.
For distinct primes p, q, …, r: d(pᵃqᵇ…rᶜ) = (a + 1)(b + 1)…(c + 1).
360 = 2³ × 3² × 5, so d(360) = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24.
Example 1: 32 = 2⁵, giving 6 factors. 75 = 3 × 5², giving 2 × 3 = 6 factors.
Example 2: Find all two-digit numbers with exactly 12 factors.
For distinct primes p, q and r, the cases are:
Factorisation of 12 | Form of n | Two-digit answers
12 | p¹¹ | Smallest is 2¹¹ = 2048, too big.
2 × 6 | p¹q⁵ | 3¹ × 2⁵ = 96
3 × 4 | p²q³ | 3² × 2³ = 72
2 × 2 × 3 | p¹q¹r² | 3 × 5 × 2² = 60; 3 × 7 × 2² = 84; 2 × 5 × 3² = 90
Thus the numbers are 60, 72, 84, 90 and 96.
notes.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.19–21

notes.heading: Gauss — Expanding and factorising
notes.body:
The distributive law pairs each term in one bracket with each term in the other: (a + b)(c + d) = ac + ad + bc + bd.
Example 1: (x + y)² = (x + y)(x + y) = x² + xy + yx + y² = x² + 2xy + y².
Example 2: (3x + y − 3)(−2x + y + 1) = −6x² + y² + xy + 9x − 2y − 3.
notes.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.34–35

notes.heading: Gauss — Pythagoras’ theorem
notes.body:
For triangle ABC with opposite sides a, b and c: a² + b² = c² if and only if angle C is a right angle.
The longest side of a right-angled triangle is called the hypotenuse.
Example 2: Sides 5, 12 and 13. Since 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13², the angle opposite the side of length 13 is a right angle. The largest angle is 90°.
For sides a, b and c opposite angles A, B and C: a² + b² > c² if and only if angle C is acute; a² + b² = c² if and only if angle C is right; a² + b² < c² if and only if angle C is obtuse.
Example 3: Explain why a triangle with sides 6, 7 and 8 must be acute-angled. Since 6² + 7² > 8², 7² + 8² > 6² and 6² + 8² > 7², each angle is acute.
notes.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.69–70

exams.title: Tech-active practice exam 1
exams.source: Written for practice, modelled on 2023–2025 Year 9 Enrichment Semester 2 tech-active exams (structure, topics and marks)
exams.instructions: Calculator allowed. These are new practice questions in the style of past exams, not copied school questions. Section marks follow the real papers: Short answer 20, Multiple choice 15, Extended response 25 (60 total). The 70-minute time is author-assigned. Answer every part. Give exact answers unless rounding is requested; retain unrounded values in intermediate calculations. Bearings are true bearings measured clockwise from north. All diagrams are described in words.

questions.prompt: 1(a) Solve x² − 3x − 28 = 0 by factorising.
questions.modelAnswer:
x² − 3x − 28 = (x + 4)(x − 7) = 0. By the null-factor law, x + 4 = 0 or x − 7 = 0.
Final answer: x = −4 or 7

questions.prompt: 1(b) The equation x² + px + 24 = 0 has solutions 3 and 8. Find p.
questions.modelAnswer:
Substitute x = 3: 9 + 3p + 24 = 0. Thus 3p = −33 and p = −11. This also gives (x − 3)(x − 8) = 0.
Final answer: p = −11

questions.prompt: 2(a) Simplify √12 + √27, giving an exact answer.
questions.modelAnswer:
√12 = 2√3 and √27 = 3√3. Add like surds: (2 + 3)√3 = 5√3.
Final answer: 5√3

questions.prompt: 2(b) Rationalise the denominator of 7/√5.
questions.modelAnswer:
Multiply numerator and denominator by √5: (7√5)/(√5√5) = 7√5/5.
Final answer: 7√5/5

questions.prompt: 3 Simplify (a³b⁴)²/(a⁵b¹⁰), using positive indices only. Assume a and b are nonzero.
questions.modelAnswer:
Apply the power rule: a⁶b⁸/(a⁵b¹⁰). Subtract indices: ab⁻². Move the negative power to the denominator.
Final answer: a/b²

questions.prompt: 4(a) A maintenance ladder is 6.4 m long. Its upper end is 3.1 m vertically above its lower end, and the ground is horizontal. Find its angle of elevation to 2 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
In the right-angled triangle, sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = 3.1/6.4. Thus θ = sin⁻¹(3.1/6.4) = 28.971532…°.
Final answer: 28.97°

questions.prompt: 4(b) A maintenance ladder is 6.4 m long. Its upper end is 3.1 m vertically above its lower end, and the ground is horizontal. Find the horizontal separation of its ends to 2 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
Let d be the horizontal separation in metres. d² + 3.1² = 6.4², so d = √(6.4² − 3.1²) = 5.599107… m. Take the positive square root because d is a length.
Final answer: 5.60 m

questions.prompt: 5 Use the quadratic formula to solve 2x² − 3x − 7 = 0. Give both solutions to 2 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
a = 2, b = −3, c = −7. The discriminant b² − 4ac = (−3)² − 4 × 2(−7) = 65. Hence x = (−(−3) ± √65)/(2 × 2). Evaluating both signs gives −1.265564… and 2.765564….
Final answer: x = −1.27 or 2.77

questions.prompt: 6 Solve 2ˣ⁺³ = 128.
questions.modelAnswer:
128 = 2⁷. Equal positive bases (not 1) have equal exponents, so x + 3 = 7. Subtract 3.
Final answer: x = 4

questions.prompt: 7 Calculate (7.24 × 10⁸)/(3.16 × 10³). Give the result in scientific notation to 3 significant figures.
questions.modelAnswer:
Use 10⁸⁻³ = 10⁵. Divide the coefficients: (7.24/3.16) × 10⁸⁻³ = 2.29113924… × 10⁵. Round the coefficient to 3 significant figures.
Final answer: 2.29 × 10⁵

questions.prompt: 1. A ground robot moves 127 m north, then 78 m east. What is its bearing from its start, to the nearest degree?
questions.explanation: tan θ = 78/127; θ = 032° clockwise from north.

questions.prompt: 2. A rectangular parcel is 4 cm by 7 cm by 9 cm. What is its longest internal diagonal?
3. The bearing of a radio mast from a hut is 126°. What is the bearing of the hut from the mast?
questions.explanation: Reverse the direction by adding 180° modulo 360°: 126° + 180° gives 306°.

questions.prompt: 4. Simplify 3√6 + 5√6.
questions.explanation: Combine like surds by adding coefficients: (3 + 5)√6 = 8√6.

questions.prompt: 5. Rationalise 5/√11.
questions.explanation: Multiply by √11/√11; the denominator becomes 11, giving 5√11/11.

questions.prompt: 6. For nonzero z, simplify z⁴ × z⁶/z².
questions.explanation: Add indices when multiplying, then subtract when dividing: 4 + 6 − 2 = 8.

questions.prompt: 7. Expand (x + 3)(x − 7).
8. Which expression equals x² − 100?
questions.explanation: This is a difference of squares: x² − 10² = (x − 10)(x + 10).

questions.prompt: 9. What is the complete solution set of x² − 12x + 32 = 0?
questions.explanation: Factorise as (x − 4)(x − 8) = 0. Both factors can be zero, so x = 4 or 8.

questions.prompt: 10. Solve 2²ˣ = 256.
questions.explanation: 256 = 2⁸, so 2x = 8, giving x = 8/2.

questions.prompt: 11. A parabola has turning point (4, −7) and one x-intercept at (10, 0). What is the x-coordinate of the other x-intercept?
questions.explanation: The axis is x = 4. Equal distances on either side give the other intercept x = 2 × 4 − 10 = −2.

questions.prompt: 12. How many distinct real solutions does x² + 5x + 25 = 0 have?
questions.explanation: The discriminant is 5² − 4(25) = −75 < 0, so there are 0 distinct real solutions.

questions.prompt: 13. A parabola has x-intercepts (−3, 0), (7, 0) and passes through (0, −42). Which is its equation?
14. What is the x-coordinate of the turning point of y = (x − 7)² + 9?
questions.explanation: Vertex form is y = (x − h)² + k, with turning point (h, k) = (7, 9).

questions.prompt: 15. Calculate (6 × 10⁵)/(2 × 10³). Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: Divide coefficients and subtract exponents: (6/2) × 10⁵⁻³ = 300.

questions.prompt: 1(a) A rectangular mural measures 9 m by 5 m. A border of uniform width x metres is added outside all four sides. Derive a simplified formula for the area A of the border only.
questions.modelAnswer:
The outer dimensions are (9 + 2x) m and (5 + 2x) m. Subtract the original area: A = (9 + 2x)(5 + 2x) − 45 = 4x² + 28x.
Final answer: A = 4x² + 28x m²

questions.prompt: 1(b) A rectangular mural measures 9 m by 5 m. A border of uniform width x metres is added outside all four sides. The border area must not exceed 72 m². Find the valid interval for x, allowing x = 0, and justify both bounds.
questions.modelAnswer:
As x is a width, x ≥ 0. The area condition is 4x² + 28x ≤ 72, so 4(x − 2)(x + 9) ≤ 0. The quadratic opens upward, so its algebraic interval lies between the roots −9 and 2. Intersect with x ≥ 0.
Final answer: 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 m

questions.prompt: 1(c) A rectangular mural measures 9 m by 5 m. A border of uniform width x metres is added outside all four sides. Find the border width if its area is 32 m². Reject any invalid solution.
questions.modelAnswer:
4x² + 28x = 32, so 4(x − 1)(x + 8) = 0. Hence x = 1 or x = −8. A negative width is impossible, so only the positive solution is valid.
Final answer: x = 1 m

questions.prompt: 2(a) A survey rover travels from base A 36 km due east to B, then 68 km on bearing 135° to C. Treat the terrain as a horizontal plane. Find how far east and how far south C is from A, both to 2 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
The second leg has east component 68 sin 135° and north component 68 cos 135°. Thus total east = 36 + 68 sin 135° = 84.08326112… km. Total south = −68 cos 135° = 48.08326112… km.
Final answer: east 84.08 km; south 48.08 km

questions.prompt: 2(b) A survey rover travels from base A 36 km due east to B, then 68 km on bearing 135° to C. Treat the terrain as a horizontal plane. Find the bearing of C from A, to the nearest whole degree.
questions.modelAnswer:
Using unrounded components E = 84.08326112… and S = 48.08326112…, C is southeast of A. The angle east of south is tan⁻¹(E/S) = 60.23679210…°. The true bearing is 180° − 60.23679210…° = 119.76320790…°.
Final answer: 120°

questions.prompt: 2(c) A survey rover travels from base A 36 km due east to B, then 68 km on bearing 135° to C. Treat the terrain as a horizontal plane. It returns directly from C to A at 84 km/h. Find the direct distance to 2 decimal places and return time to the nearest minute.
questions.modelAnswer:
Using unrounded components, AC = √(E² + S²) = 96.86069792… km. Time = distance/speed = 96.86069792…/84 hours. Multiply by 60 to obtain 69.18621280… minutes; round only at the end.
Final answer: 96.86 km; 69 minutes

questions.prompt: 3(a) A parabola crosses the x-axis at (−3, 0) and (5, 0), and passes through (0, −30). Find its equation in expanded form.
questions.modelAnswer:
Use y = a(x − (−3))(x − 5). At x = 0, −30 = −15a, so a = 2. Therefore y = 2(x + 3)(x − 5). Expanding gives 2x² − 4x − 30.
Final answer: y = 2x² − 4x − 30

questions.prompt: 3(b) For y = 2x² − 4x − 30, find the turning point, axis of symmetry and whether the turning point is a maximum or minimum.
questions.modelAnswer:
The roots are −3 and 5, so the axis is midway between them: x = (−3 + 5)/2 = 1. Substitute x = 1: y = 2(4)(−4) = −32. Since the coefficient 2 of x² is positive, the parabola opens upward.
Final answer: turning point (1, −32); axis x = 1; minimum

questions.prompt: 4 The inside of a jewellery box is a rectangular prism 7 cm long, 11 cm wide and 13 cm high. What is the maximum length of a straight rigid rod that fits fully inside, to 2 decimal places? Ignore the rod’s thickness.
questions.modelAnswer:
The floor diagonal has square 7² + 11² = 170. Apply Pythagoras again with height 13: d² = 170 + 13² = 339. The longest rod lies along a space diagonal, so d = √339 = 18.41195264… cm.
Final answer: 18.41 cm

questions.prompt: 5 An observer on a lighthouse balcony, 46 m vertically above level ground, sees a marker at an angle of depression of 29°. Find both the horizontal ground distance to the marker and the straight line-of-sight distance, to 2 decimal places. Ignore eye-height adjustments.
questions.modelAnswer:
The angle of elevation from the marker equals 29° because the horizontals are parallel. For ground distance d, tan 29° = 46/d, so d = 46/tan 29° = 82.98619674… m. For line-of-sight distance s, sin 29° = 46/s, so s = 46/sin 29° = 94.88260562… m.
Final answer: ground 82.99 m; line of sight 94.88 m

exams.instructions: Calculator allowed. These are new practice questions in the style of past exams, not copied school questions. Section marks follow the real papers: Short answer 20, Multiple choice 15, Extended response 25 (60 total). The 70-minute time is author-assigned. Answer every part. Give exact answers unless rounding is requested; retain unrounded values in intermediate calculations. Bearings are true bearings measured clockwise from north. All diagrams are described in words.

questions.prompt: 1(a) Solve x² − 4x − 60 = 0 by factorising.
questions.modelAnswer:
x² − 4x − 60 = (x + 6)(x − 10) = 0. By the null-factor law, x + 6 = 0 or x − 10 = 0.
Final answer: x = −6 or 10

questions.prompt: 1(b) The equation x² + px + 44 = 0 has solutions 4 and 11. Find p.
questions.modelAnswer:
Substitute x = 4: 16 + 4p + 44 = 0. Thus 4p = −60 and p = −15. This also gives (x − 4)(x − 11) = 0.
Final answer: p = −15

questions.prompt: 2(a) Simplify √18 + √32, giving an exact answer.
questions.modelAnswer:
√18 = 3√2 and √32 = 4√2. Add like surds: (3 + 4)√2 = 7√2.
Final answer: 7√2

questions.prompt: 2(b) Rationalise the denominator of 11/√7.
questions.modelAnswer:
Multiply numerator and denominator by √7: (11√7)/(√7√7) = 11√7/7.
Final answer: 11√7/7

questions.prompt: 3 Simplify (a⁵b³)²/(a⁷b¹⁰), using positive indices only. Assume a and b are nonzero.
questions.modelAnswer:
Apply the power rule: a¹⁰b⁶/(a⁷b¹⁰). Subtract indices: a³b⁻⁴. Move the negative power to the denominator.
Final answer: a³/b⁴

questions.prompt: 4(a) A loading ramp is 7.3 m long. Its upper end is 4.2 m vertically above its lower end, and the ground is horizontal. Find its angle of elevation to 2 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
In the right-angled triangle, sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = 4.2/7.3. Thus θ = sin⁻¹(4.2/7.3) = 35.123619…°.
Final answer: 35.12°

questions.prompt: 4(b) A loading ramp is 7.3 m long. Its upper end is 4.2 m vertically above its lower end, and the ground is horizontal. Find the horizontal separation of its ends to 2 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
Let d be the horizontal separation in metres. d² + 4.2² = 7.3², so d = √(7.3² − 4.2²) = 5.970762… m. Take the positive square root because d is a length.
Final answer: 5.97 m

questions.prompt: 5 Use the quadratic formula to solve 3x² + 5x − 9 = 0. Give both solutions to 2 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
a = 3, b = 5, c = −9. The discriminant b² − 4ac = (5)² − 4 × 3(−9) = 133. Hence x = (−(5) ± √133)/(2 × 3). Evaluating both signs gives −2.755427… and 1.088760….
Final answer: x = −2.76 or 1.09

questions.prompt: 6 Solve 2ˣ⁺⁴ = 1024.
questions.modelAnswer:
1024 = 2¹⁰. Equal positive bases (not 1) have equal exponents, so x + 4 = 10. Subtract 4.
Final answer: x = 6

questions.prompt: 7 Calculate (8.53 × 10⁹)/(4.17 × 10⁴). Give the result in scientific notation to 3 significant figures.
questions.modelAnswer:
Use 10⁹⁻⁴ = 10⁵. Divide the coefficients: (8.53/4.17) × 10⁹⁻⁴ = 2.04556355… × 10⁵. Round the coefficient to 3 significant figures.
Final answer: 2.05 × 10⁵

questions.prompt: 1. A ground robot moves 144 m north, then 91 m east. What is its bearing from its start, to the nearest degree?
questions.explanation: tan θ = 91/144; θ = 032° clockwise from north.

questions.prompt: 2. A rectangular parcel is 5 cm by 8 cm by 10 cm. What is its longest internal diagonal?
3. The bearing of a radio mast from a hut is 165°. What is the bearing of the hut from the mast?
questions.explanation: Reverse the direction by adding 180° modulo 360°: 165° + 180° gives 345°.

questions.prompt: 4. Simplify 4√10 + 6√10.
questions.explanation: Combine like surds by adding coefficients: (4 + 6)√10 = 10√10.

questions.prompt: 5. Rationalise 6/√13.
questions.explanation: Multiply by √13/√13; the denominator becomes 13, giving 6√13/13.

questions.prompt: 6. For nonzero z, simplify z⁵ × z⁷/z³.
questions.explanation: Add indices when multiplying, then subtract when dividing: 5 + 7 − 3 = 9.

questions.prompt: 7. Expand (x + 4)(x − 8).
8. Which expression equals x² − 121?
questions.explanation: This is a difference of squares: x² − 11² = (x − 11)(x + 11).

questions.prompt: 9. What is the complete solution set of x² − 14x + 45 = 0?
questions.explanation: Factorise as (x − 5)(x − 9) = 0. Both factors can be zero, so x = 5 or 9.

questions.prompt: 10. Solve 2²ˣ = 512.
questions.explanation: 512 = 2⁹, so 2x = 9, giving x = 9/2.

questions.prompt: 11. A parabola has turning point (5, −8) and one x-intercept at (13, 0). What is the x-coordinate of the other x-intercept?
questions.explanation: The axis is x = 5. Equal distances on either side give the other intercept x = 2 × 5 − 13 = −3.

questions.prompt: 12. How many distinct real solutions does x² + 12x + 36 = 0 have?
questions.explanation: The discriminant is 12² − 4(36) = 0 = 0, so there is 1 distinct real solution.

questions.prompt: 13. A parabola has x-intercepts (−4, 0), (8, 0) and passes through (0, −96). Which is its equation?
14. What is the x-coordinate of the turning point of y = (x − 8)² + 10?
questions.explanation: Vertex form is y = (x − h)² + k, with turning point (h, k) = (8, 10).

questions.prompt: 15. Calculate (12 × 10⁶)/(3 × 10⁴). Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: Divide coefficients and subtract exponents: (12/3) × 10⁶⁻⁴ = 400.

questions.prompt: 1(a) A wildlife shelter uses 34 m of fencing to enclose three sides of a rectangular exercise pen against a straight wall. The two sides perpendicular to the wall each have length x metres; the remaining fenced side has length y metres. Express y in terms of x and derive a simplified formula for the area A.
questions.modelAnswer:
The three fenced sides total 34 m, so 2x + y = 34 and y = 34 − 2x. Area = length × width, so A = x(34 − 2x) = 34x − 2x².
Final answer: y = 34 − 2x m; A = 34x − 2x² m²

questions.prompt: 1(b) A wildlife shelter uses 34 m of fencing to enclose three sides of a rectangular exercise pen against a straight wall. The two sides perpendicular to the wall each have length x metres; the remaining fenced side has length y metres. State the valid interval for x for a non-degenerate pen, and find the greatest possible area.
questions.modelAnswer:
Both lengths must be positive: x > 0 and 34 − 2x > 0, giving 0 < x < 17. Complete the square: A = −2(x − 8.5)² + 144.5. The squared term is nonnegative, so A is at most 144.5 m², attained when x = 8.5 m (and y = 17 m).
Final answer: 0 < x < 17 m; maximum area 144.5 m² at x = 8.5 m

questions.prompt: 1(c) A wildlife shelter uses 34 m of fencing to enclose three sides of a rectangular exercise pen against a straight wall. The two sides perpendicular to the wall each have length x metres; the remaining fenced side has length y metres. Find all possible values of x if the pen has area 120 m². Explain whether each is valid.
questions.modelAnswer:
34x − 2x² = 120. Rearrange and divide by −2: x² − 17x + 60 = 0. Factorise: (x − 5)(x − 12) = 0. Thus x = 5 or x = 12. Both satisfy 0 < x < 17; the corresponding lengths y are 24 m and 10 m, so both pens are valid.
Final answer: x = 5 m or 12 m

questions.prompt: 2(a) A delivery aircraft travels from base A 43 km due east to B, then 76 km on bearing 120° to C. Treat the terrain as a horizontal plane. Find how far east and how far south C is from A, both to 2 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
The second leg has east component 76 sin 120° and north component 76 cos 120°. Thus total east = 43 + 76 sin 120° = 108.81793069… km. Total south = −76 cos 120° = 38.00000000… km.
Final answer: east 108.82 km; south 38.00 km

questions.prompt: 2(b) A delivery aircraft travels from base A 43 km due east to B, then 76 km on bearing 120° to C. Treat the terrain as a horizontal plane. Find the bearing of C from A, to the nearest whole degree.
questions.modelAnswer:
Using unrounded components E = 108.81793069… and S = 38.00000000…, C is southeast of A. The angle east of south is tan⁻¹(E/S) = 70.75043297…°. The true bearing is 180° − 70.75043297…° = 109.24956703…°.
Final answer: 109°

questions.prompt: 2(c) A delivery aircraft travels from base A 43 km due east to B, then 76 km on bearing 120° to C. Treat the terrain as a horizontal plane. It returns directly from C to A at 95 km/h. Find the direct distance to 2 decimal places and return time to the nearest minute.
questions.modelAnswer:
Using unrounded components, AC = √(E² + S²) = 115.26205811… km. Time = distance/speed = 115.26205811…/95 hours. Multiply by 60 to obtain 72.79708933… minutes; round only at the end.
Final answer: 115.26 km; 73 minutes

questions.prompt: 3(a) A parabola crosses the x-axis at (−5, 0) and (9, 0), and passes through (0, −135). Find its equation in expanded form.
questions.modelAnswer:
Use y = a(x − (−5))(x − 9). At x = 0, −135 = −45a, so a = 3. Therefore y = 3(x + 5)(x − 9). Expanding gives 3x² − 12x − 135.
Final answer: y = 3x² − 12x − 135

questions.prompt: 3(b) For y = 3x² − 12x − 135, find the turning point, axis of symmetry and whether the turning point is a maximum or minimum.
questions.modelAnswer:
The roots are −5 and 9, so the axis is midway between them: x = (−5 + 9)/2 = 2. Substitute x = 2: y = 3(7)(−7) = −147. Since the coefficient 3 of x² is positive, the parabola opens upward.
Final answer: turning point (2, −147); axis x = 2; minimum

questions.prompt: 4 Solve 2³ˣ⁻² = 8192, showing your exponent working.
questions.modelAnswer:
8192 = 2¹³. Since equal powers of base 2 have equal exponents, 3x − 2 = 13. Hence 3x = 15 and x = 5.
Final answer: x = 5

questions.prompt: 5 A radio command travels 4.68 × 10⁸ m to a space probe at a constant speed of 2.40 × 10⁸ m/s. The probe replies immediately over the same distance at the same speed. Calculate the one-way travel time and the total time until the reply returns. Give both times to 3 significant figures.
questions.modelAnswer:
Time = distance/speed. One-way time = (4.68 × 10⁸)/(2.40 × 10⁸) = (4.68/2.40) × 10⁸⁻⁸ = 1.95 s. The round trip covers twice the distance, so total time = 2(1.95) = 3.90 s to 3 significant figures.
Final answer: one-way 1.95 s; round trip 3.90 s

exams.title: Tech-active practice exam 3
exams.source: Written for practice, modelled on 2023–2025 Year 9 Enrichment Semester 2 tech-active exams (structure, topics and marks)
exams.instructions: Calculator allowed. These are new practice questions in the style of past exams, not copied school questions. Section marks follow the real papers: Short answer 20, Multiple choice 15, Extended response 25 (60 total). The 70-minute time is author-assigned. Answer every part. Give exact answers unless rounding is requested; retain unrounded values in intermediate calculations. Bearings are true bearings measured clockwise from north. All diagrams are described in words.

questions.prompt: 1(a) Solve x² − 2x − 99 = 0 by factorising.
questions.modelAnswer:
x² − 2x − 99 = (x + 9)(x − 11) = 0. By the null-factor law, x + 9 = 0 or x − 11 = 0.
Final answer: x = −9 or 11

questions.prompt: 1(b) The equation x² + px + 60 = 0 has solutions 5 and 12. Find p.
questions.modelAnswer:
Substitute x = 5: 25 + 5p + 60 = 0. Thus 5p = −85 and p = −17. This also gives (x − 5)(x − 12) = 0.
Final answer: p = −17

questions.prompt: 2(a) Simplify √80 + √125, giving an exact answer.
questions.modelAnswer:
√80 = 4√5 and √125 = 5√5. Add like surds: (4 + 5)√5 = 9√5.
Final answer: 9√5

questions.prompt: 2(b) Rationalise the denominator of 13/√3.
questions.modelAnswer:
Multiply numerator and denominator by √3: (13√3)/(√3√3) = 13√3/3.
Final answer: 13√3/3

questions.prompt: 3 Simplify (a⁴b⁵)²/(a⁶b¹³), using positive indices only. Assume a and b are nonzero.
questions.modelAnswer:
Apply the power rule: a⁸b¹⁰/(a⁶b¹³). Subtract indices: a²b⁻³. Move the negative power to the denominator.
Final answer: a²/b³

questions.prompt: 4(a) A rescue gangway is 8.6 m long. Its upper end is 5.3 m vertically above its lower end, and the ground is horizontal. Find its angle of elevation to 2 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
In the right-angled triangle, sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = 5.3/8.6. Thus θ = sin⁻¹(5.3/8.6) = 38.044919…°.
Final answer: 38.04°

questions.prompt: 4(b) A rescue gangway is 8.6 m long. Its upper end is 5.3 m vertically above its lower end, and the ground is horizontal. Find the horizontal separation of its ends to 2 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
Let d be the horizontal separation in metres. d² + 5.3² = 8.6², so d = √(8.6² − 5.3²) = 6.772739… m. Take the positive square root because d is a length.
Final answer: 6.77 m

questions.prompt: 5 Use the quadratic formula to solve 4x² − 7x − 6 = 0. Give both solutions to 2 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
a = 4, b = −7, c = −6. The discriminant b² − 4ac = (−7)² − 4 × 4(−6) = 145. Hence x = (−(−7) ± √145)/(2 × 4). Evaluating both signs gives −0.630199… and 2.380199….
Final answer: x = −0.63 or 2.38

questions.prompt: 6 Solve 2ˣ⁺⁵ = 4096.
questions.modelAnswer:
4096 = 2¹². Equal positive bases (not 1) have equal exponents, so x + 5 = 12. Subtract 5.
Final answer: x = 7

questions.prompt: 7 Calculate (6.91 × 10¹⁰)/(2.73 × 10⁵). Give the result in scientific notation to 3 significant figures.
questions.modelAnswer:
Use 10¹⁰⁻⁵ = 10⁵. Divide the coefficients: (6.91/2.73) × 10¹⁰⁻⁵ = 2.53113553… × 10⁵. Round the coefficient to 3 significant figures.
Final answer: 2.53 × 10⁵

questions.prompt: 1. A ground robot moves 161 m north, then 104 m east. What is its bearing from its start, to the nearest degree?
questions.explanation: tan θ = 104/161; θ = 033° clockwise from north.

questions.prompt: 2. A rectangular parcel is 6 cm by 9 cm by 11 cm. What is its longest internal diagonal?
3. The bearing of a radio mast from a hut is 204°. What is the bearing of the hut from the mast?
questions.explanation: Reverse the direction by adding 180° modulo 360°: 204° + 180° gives 024°.

questions.prompt: 4. Simplify 5√7 + 7√7.
questions.explanation: Combine like surds by adding coefficients: (5 + 7)√7 = 12√7.

questions.prompt: 5. Rationalise 7/√17.
questions.explanation: Multiply by √17/√17; the denominator becomes 17, giving 7√17/17.

questions.prompt: 6. For nonzero z, simplify z⁶ × z⁸/z⁴.
questions.explanation: Add indices when multiplying, then subtract when dividing: 6 + 8 − 4 = 10.

questions.prompt: 7. Expand (x + 5)(x − 9).
8. Which expression equals x² − 144?
questions.explanation: This is a difference of squares: x² − 12² = (x − 12)(x + 12).

questions.prompt: 9. What is the complete solution set of x² − 16x + 60 = 0?
questions.explanation: Factorise as (x − 6)(x − 10) = 0. Both factors can be zero, so x = 6 or 10.

questions.prompt: 10. Solve 2²ˣ = 1024.
questions.explanation: 1024 = 2¹⁰, so 2x = 10, giving x = 10/2.

questions.prompt: 11. A parabola has turning point (6, −9) and one x-intercept at (16, 0). What is the x-coordinate of the other x-intercept?
questions.explanation: The axis is x = 6. Equal distances on either side give the other intercept x = 2 × 6 − 16 = −4.

questions.prompt: 12. How many distinct real solutions does x² + 9x + 14 = 0 have?
questions.explanation: The discriminant is 9² − 4(14) = 25 > 0, so there are 2 distinct real solutions.

questions.prompt: 13. A parabola has x-intercepts (−5, 0), (9, 0) and passes through (0, −180). Which is its equation?
14. What is the x-coordinate of the turning point of y = (x − 9)² + 11?
questions.explanation: Vertex form is y = (x − h)² + k, with turning point (h, k) = (9, 11).

questions.prompt: 15. Calculate (20 × 10⁷)/(4 × 10⁵). Which value is correct?
questions.explanation: Divide coefficients and subtract exponents: (20/4) × 10⁷⁻⁵ = 500.

questions.prompt: 1(a) A rectangular display platform measures 14 m by 9 m. A border of uniform width x metres is added outside all four sides. Derive a simplified formula for the area A of the border only.
questions.modelAnswer:
The outer dimensions are (14 + 2x) m and (9 + 2x) m. Subtract the original area: A = (14 + 2x)(9 + 2x) − 126 = 4x² + 46x.
Final answer: A = 4x² + 46x m²

questions.prompt: 1(b) A rectangular display platform measures 14 m by 9 m. A border of uniform width x metres is added outside all four sides. The border area must not exceed 248 m². Find the valid interval for x, allowing x = 0, and justify both bounds.
questions.modelAnswer:
As x is a width, x ≥ 0. The area condition is 4x² + 46x ≤ 248, so 4(x − 4)(x + 31/2) ≤ 0. The quadratic opens upward, so its algebraic interval lies between the roots −31/2 and 4. Intersect with x ≥ 0.
Final answer: 0 ≤ x ≤ 4 m

questions.prompt: 1(c) A rectangular display platform measures 14 m by 9 m. A border of uniform width x metres is added outside all four sides. Find the border width if its area is 174 m². Reject any invalid solution.
questions.modelAnswer:
4x² + 46x = 174, so 4(x − 3)(x + 29/2) = 0. Hence x = 3 or x = −29/2. A negative width is impossible, so only the positive solution is valid.
Final answer: x = 3 m

questions.prompt: 2(a) A research boat travels from base A 57 km due east to B, then 92 km on bearing 150° to C. Treat the terrain as a horizontal plane. Find how far east and how far south C is from A, both to 2 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
The second leg has east component 92 sin 150° and north component 92 cos 150°. Thus total east = 57 + 92 sin 150° = 103.00000000… km. Total south = −92 cos 150° = 79.67433715… km.
Final answer: east 103.00 km; south 79.67 km

questions.prompt: 2(b) A research boat travels from base A 57 km due east to B, then 92 km on bearing 150° to C. Treat the terrain as a horizontal plane. Find the bearing of C from A, to the nearest whole degree.
questions.modelAnswer:
Using unrounded components E = 103.00000000… and S = 79.67433715…, C is southeast of A. The angle east of south is tan⁻¹(E/S) = 52.27671307…°. The true bearing is 180° − 52.27671307…° = 127.72328693…°.
Final answer: 128°

questions.prompt: 2(c) A research boat travels from base A 57 km due east to B, then 92 km on bearing 150° to C. Treat the terrain as a horizontal plane. It returns directly from C to A at 110 km/h. Find the direct distance to 2 decimal places and return time to the nearest minute.
questions.modelAnswer:
Using unrounded components, AC = √(E² + S²) = 130.21904623… km. Time = distance/speed = 130.21904623…/110 hours. Multiply by 60 to obtain 71.02857067… minutes; round only at the end.
Final answer: 130.22 km; 71 minutes

questions.prompt: 3(a) A laboratory culture starts with 720 cells and grows by 25% every hour. Write a model N(t) for its population after t hours, assuming exponential growth. Estimate the population after 4 hours, to the nearest whole cell.
questions.modelAnswer:
An increase of 25% multiplies the population by 1 + 25/100 = 1.25 each hour. Therefore N(t) = 720(1.25)ᵗ. At t = 4, N(4) = 720(1.25)⁴ = 1757.8125. Round to a whole number of cells.
Final answer: N(t) = 720(1.25)ᵗ; 1758 cells

questions.prompt: 3(b) The model for a culture is N(t) = 720(1.25)ᵗ, where t is measured in hours. Using calculator trials or a table of values, find the first whole number of hours after which the culture exceeds 3600 cells.
questions.modelAnswer:
Use calculator trials in N(t) = 720(1.25)ᵗ. N(7) = 720(1.25)⁷ ≈ 3433.23 cells, which is below 3600. N(8) = 720(1.25)⁸ ≈ 4291.53 cells, which exceeds 3600. Since the population is multiplied by 1.25 each hour, it increases. Therefore 7 hours is too early and 8 is the first whole number of hours that works.
Final answer: 8 hours

questions.prompt: 4 A rectangular crate has internal length 18 cm and width 22 cm. Its longest internal diagonal is 31 cm. Find its internal height to 2 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
For a rectangular prism, d² = l² + w² + h². Hence h² = 31² − 18² − 22² = 961 − 324 − 484 = 153. A height is positive, so h = √153 = 3√17 = 12.369316… cm.
Final answer: 12.37 cm

questions.prompt: 5 An observer on an observation tower, 68 m vertically above level ground, sees a marker at an angle of depression of 41°. Find both the horizontal ground distance to the marker and the straight line-of-sight distance, to 2 decimal places. Ignore eye-height adjustments.
questions.modelAnswer:
The angle of elevation from the marker equals 41° because the horizontals are parallel. For ground distance d, tan 41° = 68/d, so d = 68/tan 41° = 78.22505169… m. For line-of-sight distance s, sin 41° = 68/s, so s = 68/sin 41° = 103.64920990… m.
Final answer: ground 78.23 m; line of sight 103.65 m

exams.title: Gauss — Worked examples (Practice paper 1)
exams.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.1–3, 21, 35, 70
exams.instructions: These questions are Gauss worked examples. The worked solutions also appear in the Notes, so attempt each question before reading them. Marks (2–3 per question) and time are author-assigned for self-practice, not an exam prediction.

questions.prompt: Gauss p.1, Example 1. Find the 100th term of {1, 4, 7, 10, …}.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf p.1

questions.prompt: Gauss p.2, Example 2. The 8th term of an arithmetic sequence is 50 and the 20th term is 14. Find the first term.
questions.modelAnswer: 50 = a + 7d and 14 = a + 19d. Subtracting gives 12d = −36, so d = −3. Then a = 50 + 21 = 71.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf p.2

questions.prompt: Gauss p.2, Example 3. For {13, 7, 1, −5, …}, find the sum of the first 49 terms.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf p.2

questions.prompt: Gauss p.3, Example 4. Find the 15th term of {768, 384, 192, …}.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf p.3

questions.prompt: Gauss p.3, Example 5. The 20th and 23rd terms are 24 and 648. Find the common ratio.
questions.modelAnswer: 24 = ar¹⁹ and 648 = ar²². Divide: r³ = 648 ÷ 24 = 27. Therefore r = 3.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf p.3

questions.prompt: Gauss p.3, Example 6. Find x in the geometric sequence {…, 5, x, 245, …}.
questions.modelAnswer: 5r² = 245, so r² = 49, giving r = 7 or −7. Therefore x = 35 or −35.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf p.3

questions.prompt: Gauss p.21, Example 1. Show that 32 and 75 have the same numbers of factors.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf p.21

questions.prompt: Gauss p.21, Example 2. Find all two-digit numbers with exactly 12 factors.
questions.modelAnswer:
For distinct primes p, q and r, the cases are:
Factorisation of 12 | Form of n | Two-digit answers
12 | p¹¹ | Smallest is 2¹¹ = 2048, too big.
2 × 6 | p¹q⁵ | 3¹ × 2⁵ = 96
3 × 4 | p²q³ | 3² × 2³ = 72
2 × 2 × 3 | p¹q¹r² | 3 × 5 × 2² = 60; 3 × 7 × 2² = 84; 2 × 5 × 3² = 90
Thus the numbers are 60, 72, 84, 90 and 96.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf p.21

questions.prompt: Gauss p.35, Example 1. Expand and simplify (x + y)².
questions.modelAnswer: (x + y)(x + y) = x² + xy + yx + y² = x² + 2xy + y².
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf p.35

questions.prompt: Gauss p.35, Example 2. Expand and simplify (3x + y − 3)(−2x + y + 1).
questions.modelAnswer: −6x² + 3xy + 3x − 2xy + y² + y + 6x − 3y − 3 = −6x² + y² + xy + 9x − 2y − 3.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf p.35

questions.prompt: Gauss p.70, Example 2. What is the largest angle in a triangle with sides 5, 12 and 13?
questions.modelAnswer: 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13². There is a right angle opposite the side of length 13. The largest angle is 90°.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf p.70

questions.prompt: Gauss p.70, Example 3. Explain why a triangle with sides 6, 7 and 8 must be acute-angled.
questions.modelAnswer: Since 6² + 7² > 8², 7² + 8² > 6² and 6² + 8² > 7², each angle is acute.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf p.70

questions.prompt: Find all possible values of the first term of a geometric sequence, given t₃ = 500 and t₇ = 312 500.
questions.modelAnswer: r⁴ = t₇ ÷ t₃ = 312 500 ÷ 500 = 625, so r = 5 or r = −5 (since the index is even). For either value, a = t₃ ÷ r² = 500 ÷ 25 = 20. There are two different geometric sequences, with the same first term.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.4, 89

questions.prompt: The population of a species increases by 5% each year. How many years will it take for the population to be at least double its original size?
questions.modelAnswer: After n years, the population increases by a factor of 1.05ⁿ. We need the least n for which this factor is at least 2. By guess-and-check, 1.05¹⁴ ≈ 1.98 and 1.05¹⁵ ≈ 2.08. So it will take 15 years.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.4, 89

questions.prompt: How many factors does 5² × 9³ × 13⁴ have?
questions.modelAnswer: 9 is not prime, so write 9³ as (3²)³ = 3⁶. Then d(3⁶ × 5² × 13⁴) = (6 + 1) × (2 + 1) × (4 + 1) = 7 × 3 × 5 = 105.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.21, 97

questions.prompt: Which number has more factors: 3 million or 4 million?
questions.modelAnswer: 1 000 000 = 10⁶ = (2 × 5)⁶ = 2⁶ × 5⁶. Therefore d(3 000 000) = d(2⁶ × 3¹ × 5⁶) = 7 × 2 × 7 = 98, and d(4 000 000) = d(2⁸ × 5⁶) = 9 × 7 = 63. So 3 million has more factors than 4 million.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.21, 97

questions.prompt: Find the smallest number with exactly 55 factors.
questions.modelAnswer: A number with 55 factors has the form p⁵⁴ or p⁴q¹⁰. The number 2⁵⁴ has 17 digits. For the other form, letting p = 3 and q = 2 gives 3⁴ × 2¹⁰ = 82 944, which is considerably smaller!
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.21, 97

questions.prompt: An even number has exactly 27 factors, one of which is 117. Find the number.
questions.modelAnswer: The number is even, so 2 is one prime factor. Also, 117 = 9 × 13 = 3² × 13, so 3 and 13 are another two prime factors. A number with 27 factors has the form p²⁶, p²q⁸ or p²q²r². Rule out the first two because there are at least three prime factors. So the number is 2² × 3² × 13² = 6084.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.21, 97

questions.prompt:
Expand and simplify each of the following.
(a) (x − y)²
questions.modelAnswer: (x − y)² = (x − y)(x − y) = x² − xy − yx + y² = x² − 2xy + y².

questions.prompt: Describe all possible right-angled triangles with one side of length 20 and another side of length 21.
questions.modelAnswer: By SSS congruence, specify all three side lengths. If 20 and 21 are the short sides, c² = 20² + 21² = 400 + 441 = 841, so c = √841 = 29. If 21 is the hypotenuse, b² = 21² − 20² = 441 − 400 = 41, so b = √41 (≈ 6.40).
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.71, 122

questions.prompt: A triangle has sides of length 23, 31 and 41. What kinds of angles does it have?
questions.modelAnswer: Since 23² + 31² = 529 + 961 = 1490 < 1681 = 41², the angle opposite the side of length 41 is obtuse, and the other two angles must be acute.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.71, 122

questions.prompt: An isosceles triangle has base length 6 and area 12. What is its perimeter?
questions.modelAnswer: From A = ½bh, 12 = ½ × 6 × h, so h = 4. Split the isosceles triangle into two congruent right-angled triangles with short sides ½b = 3 and h = 4. By Pythagoras’ theorem each hypotenuse is 5. The perimeter is 6 + 2 × 5 = 16.
questions.source: 2026 Maths Enrichment Gauss Student Notes.pdf pp.71, 122
